newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters sees back of govt talks broken by Mon.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters sees back of govt talks broken by Mon.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters on Wednesday said he expects the back of coalition talks with the conservative caretaker National government and the centre-left Labour Party to be broken by Monday.

Peters told a news conference that further informal talks would continue this week and NZ First we re-enter formal talks with both parties next week. He said it would be wrong to assume that NZ First was siding with either National or Labour.
Peters declined to give a timetable of when a government might ber formed.
NZ First holds the balance of power after inconclusive elections last month and has been negotiating with both the National caretaker government and the Labour opposition party to form a coalition.

Peters said when negotiations were complete, two propositions would be presented to the NZ First Party caucus. He said he expected the caucus would then take less than a week to decide on who to form a government with and a decision would be made by consensus.
"We don't intend to put it to the vote, we would like to put it to a consesus," Peters said.
He said informal talks today covered 10 issues. "From all reports progress was very, very good," he said.
Peters said there were minimal areas of difference between NZ First and Labour or National.

He said if an agreement was reached with Labour, then Labour would have to reach an understanding with the left-wing Alliance party, which has 13 seats in parliament. Labour would have to get the Alliance's support before NZ First would decide which way to go.
"To be safe, you would have to ensure you have the Alliance's undertaking before you made that ultimate commitment," Peters said. "We don't believe in testing the water with both feet."
In the October 12 election, National won 44 seats, Labour 37, New Zealand First 17, the Alliance 13, radical free-market ACT eight and the centrist United Party one.
To govern, Labour and NZ First would need the support of the Alliance party although it has said it would remain outside a coalition.
